bpf_evidence_note.detail: Latest strict BPF artifact has global counters but lacks successful-path per-interface seen/redirect counters required by the gate.
bpf_evidence_note.status: remaining evidence blocker, not changed in this goal

decision: workload catalog must be redesigned before any 300+ run

fix_options.tradeoff: Longer S4 horizon improves center coverage for North America East, but 600s still has zero common zone/UT candidates and zero G/Z FEC, so this is insufficient alone.
Can create a bounded gate sooner by requiring only spatially coherent zones, but weakens broad workload representativeness.
Splitting wide regions or selecting anchors from coherent UT clusters preserves semantics better than allowing one anchor to cover globally scattered UTs.
Useful after anchors resolve, but current failure occurs before gateway-path scoring for all required samples except short-window North America East margin cases.
S3/720 120s adds density and center coverage, but still has zero common zone/UT candidates and zero G/Z FEC with this catalog.
Reclassify remote-return/boundary cases or use smaller per-zone UT sets, but do so explicitly because it changes the gate workload.

fix_options.option: keep S4 with a different workload catalog
fix_options.tradeoff: Best route if S4 remains the target: use catalog/effective coordinates consistently or disable shell-aware relocation for realistic catalog previews.

primary_blocker: Required service-zone anchor policy requires one satellite that clears the zone-center threshold and is visible to every UT in the zone. With shell-aware effective ground placement, required-zone UTs are thousands of kilometers from their fixed zone centers, producing zero common zone/UT candidates.
